description: Contracting-authority profiles not yet pinned for ČEB, ČSSZ, Ministerstvo vnitra, Finanční správa, Celní správa, Státní pokladna Centrum sdílených služeb (SPCSS), and regional/municipal treasuries.
No CPV code list was fixed for banking/payments scope (e.g. 66-series financial services, 72-series IT services, 30144/30162 cash-register and card equipment, 48-series software packages).
TED (EU Tenders Electronic Daily) was not covered in this cell, although Czech above-threshold notices are duplicated there in structured, multilingual, bulk-downloadable form.
Procurement-quality/analytics projects (e.g. zIndex, Otevřená smlouva/Otevřená data initiatives, EDZ analyses) were not enumerated.
Bulk/API access terms unknown for NEN, VVZ and Tender arena; only Registr smluv (NKOD) and Hlídač státu are confirmed to expose machine-readable paths.

No actor map yet of the specific Czech contracting authorities most likely to buy payments/banking IT above EU threshold — beyond ČNB and Celní správa, candidates include Ministerstvo financí, Státní pokladna Centrum sdílených služeb, Česká pošta, ČSSZ, Generální finanční ředitelství, Czech regional and municipal authorities, and state-owned banks (Národní rozvojová banka, Exportní garanční a pojišťovací společnost).

The cell's premise is that TED reveals cross-border vendors (Diebold Nixdorf, NCR Atleos, Worldline, Nexi, Temenos, Fiserv) bidding into CZ, but no supplier-name-anchored searching was completed, and Czech-market incumbents were not enumerated (e.g. Monet+, ICZ, Asseco Central Europe, Aricoma/Cleverlance, Global Payments, Worldline Czech branch, Comdata).

No validated CPV whitelist for banking and payments exists yet. Only 72212443 was given as a seed; adjacent families (66100000 banking and investment services, 48xxxxxx software packages, 72xxxxxx IT services, 30xxxxxx office/cash equipment, 50xxxxxx repair and maintenance, 79xxxxxx business services) are unmapped.

Local-language coverage was achieved for procurement procedure vocabulary and funding vocabulary, but not for technical banking-IT Czech terms that would appear in tender subject lines — e.g. 'bankovní informační systém', 'karetní centrum', 'zpracování hotovosti', 'okamžité platby', 'platební styk', 'switch pro platební karty', 'AML systém', 'core banking systém'.

Oversight and audit sources that comment on EU-funded and above-threshold Czech IT contracts were not covered: ÚOHS (competition/procurement review decisions), NKÚ (Supreme Audit Office), and the European Court of Auditors. These reveal disputed and cancelled awards and named incumbents in ways award notices do not.

Specific EU programme instruments beyond DIGITAL and NPO were not examined for Czech payments relevance: IROP (e-government), OP TAK digitalisation calls, Connecting Europe Facility Digital, InvestEU / EIF guarantees to Czech fintechs, and EDIH network members in CZ.

TED API access requires EU Login and an API key, which has not been provisioned; no assessment of rate limits or of whether the API exposes historical (pre-eForms) notices with the same field fidelity.

This pass mapped the register infrastructure but did not yet materialise the actual watchlist of CZ payment institutions, e-money institutions, PSMR providers and banking-technology vendors with their IČO identifiers.
With ESM closed to the public, there is no confirmed replacement for beneficial-ownership evidence on privately held CZ fintechs whose shareholder of record is an opaque holding company.
Paid pan-European filing aggregators (Bisnode/Dun & Bradstreet CZ, Orbis/Bureau van Dijk, OpenCorporates) were inferred from first principles but not searched or priced in this pass.

Many CZ payment vendors operate as CZ/SK pairs; the Slovak counterpart registers (ORSR, RPVS register of public sector partners, Finstat) were out of the stated CZ scope but are essential to see the full group.

English-language coverage of Czech statutory filings is thin: the register front-ends offer partial English UI but filed documents (výroční zpráva, zpráva o vztazích) are essentially Czech-only, sometimes as scans.

For several directories (APEK 580+, SP ČR, HK ČR ~140 sector associations, AmCham) only the entry page was identified; pagination scheme, total record count and whether member entries carry structured metadata (sector, size, website) were not established.
No association was found that specifically organises POS/terminal, ATM or cash-handling suppliers in CZ; these vendors appear only scattered across ICT UNIE, Czech ICT Alliance and APEK.
Working-group pages were confirmed to exist for ČBA and ICT UNIE, but it is unknown whether either publishes named participant rosters or only topic descriptions and chairs.

German-language coverage was only touched via ČNOPK; the run scope is cs+en, so the German bilateral chamber's German-side content and the nemeckefirmy.cz database were not explored in their native language.
No archival strategy was established for association member lists, which are overwritten in place — so entries/exits and vendor churn cannot be reconstructed retrospectively.

This pass discovered organiser sites but did not fetch the actual partner/exhibitor/speaker pages for CARDFORUM, financnictvi.konference.cz, fintechweekcee.com, itprofinance.cz or moneyfest.cz — so no named partner rosters were extracted for those events beyond what press coverage reported.

Sponsor pages are overwritten each year; no back-year capture strategy exists for CZ events, though evidence of retrievable archives was seen (cardforum.cz/data/*.pdf, itprofinance.cz/historie/, financnictvi.konference.cz year URLs, sched.com for Money20/20 2018).

CEE coverage beyond CZ is thin: only Fintech Week CEE and one CzechTrade Budapest delegation were found. No SK/PL/HU/AT conference sponsor lists were enumerated, despite CZ vendors and banks operating regionally.

Insurance-side and building-society events are only incidentally covered (awards mention Kooperativa, Allianz, Generali Česká) even though the run scope is sector=both. No dedicated insurtech conference or exhibitor list was enumerated.

Award coverage is strong but several award programmes are reachable only through PR syndication (Visa Awards, Zlatá koruna, Finparáda), which makes the record dependent on media rewrites rather than organiser primary data.

The 'hackathon' leg of the cell is the weakest: no stable CZ bank-hackathon results or partner pages were found, and the strongest lead (Mastercard-backed FinTechers hackathon inside Fintech Week CEE, ~1M CZK prize pool) is forward-looking rather than archived.
Vendor-product keyword coverage of jobs.cz/prace.cz/StartupJobs must be done through each board's native site search, not general web search.
Employee skill profiles as a category are covered only by LinkedIn, which is blocked for automated collection.

Developer portals were enumerated for the large banks; the long tail (Fio, UniCredit CZ, Trinity Bank, Creditas, Max banka, credit unions, and non-bank PSPs GoPay/ComGate/Twisto) is not yet individually catalogued.
Engineering-community artefacts beyond job ads — CZ meetups, conference speaker lists, and their vendor sponsors — were only touched indirectly via the IT Trendy event calendar.
All URLs in this slice are search-derived and unverified for liveness; several (apiportal.cz, apiportal.moneta.cz, developers.csob.cz) were never fetched directly in this pass.
Heureka.cz merchant/product reviews and Reddit (r/czech, r/Prague, r/czechrepublic) were not yet mined for payment-failure and gateway-complaint threads in this pass.

Public procurement records (Věstník veřejných zakázek, TED) for transit/rail/municipal payment-acceptance tenders were not searched, yet they are the most reliable route to naming acquirers and terminal vendors behind transport deployments.
Other large CZ merchant groups and marketplaces were not covered: Mall/Allegro CZ, Kaufland, Billa, Tesco/Globus, Dr.Max, Datart, Zásilkovna/Packeta and Benzina/ORLEN fuel retail.
No technical checkout-fingerprinting method is yet defined for identifying a merchant's PSP from public checkout assets/domains, which is the only scalable way to fill provider-attribution gaps.

Cvak itself (the A2A scheme operator behind Albert and Lidl adoption, associated notably with Air Bank) has not had its own corporate/product site, bank partner release notes, or ČNB licence record identified.
ČOI (Česká obchodní inspekce) and the EU ODR platform were not examined as complaint channels for e-shop payment disputes.
The exact JERRS open-data p_seznam id (if any) covering platební instituce, instituce elektronických peněz, PPSMR and VEPMR was not established; only ids 1, 2, 3 and 7 were evidenced.
JERRS search/detail URL patterns were not mapped — only the login/entry URL was observed. Deep-link structure for a single entity record and for a filtered list by licence type is unknown.

AML supervision (Finanční analytický úřad, FAÚ) and cyber/ICT supervision (NÚKIB) were not searched in this slice; both regulate CZ payment providers and publish annual reports and, in FAÚ's case, guidance naming typologies and obliged-entity categories.

The relationship between the ČNB JERRS entry set and the EBA PSD2 register CZ subset (reported as ~201 entities via a third-party mirror, not verified at EBA) has not been reconciled, including passporting-in TPPs that have no CZ establishment.

Register snapshots are point-in-time; no evidence was found of a ČNB-published historical archive of register states, so entry/exit history of payment institutions cannot be reconstructed from the register alone.
No owned press-room or IR source located for Fio banka and only an inferred one for Banka CREDITAS; Air Bank's press room (as opposed to its annual-report PDFs) was also not observed.

Owned recruitment/careers channels were not explored. CZ bank job postings (kariera.csas.cz, KB, ČSOB careers, plus their LinkedIn pages) name concrete technologies — core platform, cloud provider, middleware — far more explicitly than press releases.

DORA-driven ICT third-party disclosures and outsourcing registers, and Pillar 3 / operational-risk sections of bank reports, were not separately profiled — these are the highest-density owned source of material-vendor names now in force in the EU.
No RSS/Atom feeds or structured newsroom APIs were identified for any of the press rooms profiled, so all collection is HTML-scrape based and fragile to redesign.

English-language versions of the CZ press rooms were not systematically checked; several banks publish only a subset of releases in English, and group-level English releases (Erste, KBC, SG, RBI, UniCredit) may carry vendor names dropped from the Czech text.
FIS and Fiserv were named in the cell brief but not searched individually in this pass; neither surfaced incidentally.

CZ-side actor map is thin: searches gravitated to KB, ČSOB, Česká spořitelna and Air Bank. Missing: Moneta Money Bank, Raiffeisenbank CZ, UniCredit Bank CZ, Fio banka, Trinity Bank, Banka CREDITAS, Partners Banka, Revolut/Wise CZ presence, and PSPs (GoPay, ComGate, Global Payments s.r.o., Monet+).

Hyperscaler and platform partner case studies (Microsoft, AWS, Google Cloud, Salesforce, Red Hat) were not systematically searched, yet the cs search showed Salesforce/Enehano and MS Dynamics CZ bank studies exist.
No use was made of web archives to recover withdrawn or relocated vendor case studies and reference lists.
Czech IT/banking trade media that republish vendor announcements (e.g. Lupa.cz, ChannelWorld.cz, ITBiz, SystemOnLine, Bankovnictvi/Bankovnictví magazine, Měšec.cz) were not searched.

Vendor conference and user-group programmes (Temenos Community Forum, Backbase ENGAGE, DN 'Intersect', Nexi/Worldline customer days) list speaking client banks and are an under-used route to unpublicised CZ references.

Slovak and wider CEE arms of the same integrators (Asseco SK, Trask SK, Adastra SK/PL, Monet+ SK) were not covered; CZ banks are largely subsidiaries of Austrian/Belgian/French groups and projects are often contracted or referenced regionally.
OEM/product-vendor partner directories (Camunda, Microsoft, SAP, Temenos, Diebold Nixdorf, Backbase, Salesforce) that list certified CZ implementation partners were not harvested.

Public procurement channels were not searched: Registr smluv, Věstník veřejných zakázek and NEN reveal IT contracts with state-linked financial institutions (ČNB, ČMZRB/NRB, EGAP, ČEB, Česká pošta / Poštovní spořitelna perimeter).
Only current-state pages were sampled; historical reference pages that vendors have since removed (typical after an NDA complaint or a lost account) were not retrieved.

Czech-language coverage was achieved for all major actors, but CZ/EN site trees diverge: several vendors publish different reference subsets per language, and no Slovak-language querying was done at all.

Financial-statement content was identified as a source type but no actual filing was retrieved or parsed, so revenue concentration on named bank clients remains unquantified for every actor in the cell.

International PSP entrants into CZ (Adyen, Stripe, Revolut Business, Klarna, PayU, Mollie) are not yet covered by any direct source in this slice; only third-party integration pages evidence their presence.
Account-to-account / instant payment rails competing with cards in CZ (CERTIS, okamžité platby, bank-transfer buttons, Shoptet Pay's A2A methods) were not systematically scouted in this pass.

No company-registry or financial-statement source was captured for CZ payments entities (justice.cz / obchodní rejstřík, sbírka listin), which would give ownership, group structure and revenue for gateways and terminal vendors.
Public procurement of terminals and acquiring services (NEN, Věstník veřejných zakázek, TED) was not scouted; these tenders name incumbent suppliers, contract values and renewal dates.

English-language coverage of CZ payments was thin in this pass — group-level newsrooms (Global Payments/Worldpay divestiture on Businesswire, Worldline and Mastercard Europe feeds) were touched but not systematically mapped for Czech relevance.

Public-procurement sources are entirely absent from this slice: Věstník veřejných zakázek, NEN, TED (EU), and contract registers (Registr smluv) were not searched, yet they are where infrastructure supplier selections become public.

Sector coverage is bank-centric; the cell's 'both' sector scope means non-bank payment infrastructure actors were under-covered — card scheme/ATM and switching operators active in CZ, and the CZ card-processing side generally.

Most candidate URLs come from search-result metadata rather than direct fetches; only the ČBA open-banking page was fetched in this pass. Several deep-link PDFs and registry endpoints are therefore inferred, not observed.

Case studies are the weakest of the four topics here: infrastructure operators publish rules and rosters, not implementation narratives. Only bank press releases and trade media currently carry case-study material.

Slovak-language sources were not searched even though several CZ-market institutions (e.g. UniCredit Bank Czech Republic and Slovakia) operate cross-border and publish SK-language infrastructure material.

Vendor-switch and failure vocabulary was only partially exercised: 'mění dodavatele', 'vypověděla smlouvu', 'nahradí systém', 'migrace na', 'odstavila', 'odložila spuštění', 'nasadila řešení od' were not each run as separate cs queries.

No systematic per-bank and per-vendor name sweep was run (Česká spořitelna, ČSOB, Komerční banka, Moneta, Raiffeisenbank, Air Bank/Partners Banka, Fio, Trinity, UniCredit CZ; vendors Temenos, nCino, Kyndryl, Unicorn, ICZ, Asseco, Monet+, GLOBAL PAYMENTS/Comdata, Printec peers).

Broadcast/podcast and video trade commentary (ČT24 Ekonomika, Seznam Zprávy byznys, Czech fintech podcasts, conference recordings such as Fintree/Bankovnictví awards) were not explored, although executives often disclose vendor detail on stage.
Slovak-language trade media (Trend.sk, Živé.sk, Finweb) frequently cover CZ/SK shared banking groups and their vendors, but Slovak was out of the declared language set (cs, en) and was not searched.
No URL in this slice was fetched or liveness-checked; all statuses (paywall, gating, section structure) are hypotheses derived from search snippets.

No systematic vendor-newsroom watchlist exists yet, although vendor sites (Temenos, nCino, IDEMIA, FICO, Finshape, Antelop, Global Payments) proved to be the earliest and most detailed disclosure point for CZ bank deals.

English sources render Czech bank names inconsistently — 'Ceska sporitelna' vs 'Česká spořitelna', 'Komercni banka' vs 'Komerční banka', 'Ceskoslovenska obchodni banka' vs 'ČSOB', plus one observed misspelling 'Czechzia' in a headline. Naive keyword matching will miss items.

Seznam-independent CEE English outlets beyond bne IntelliNews (e.g. Emerging Europe, CEE fintech newsletters, Finovate regional coverage) were only lightly sampled; their CZ-specific yield is unassessed.

No credible aggregate view of CZ banking/payments vendor market shares was identified; only vendor-count proxies (IBSi Sales League Table) and generic market-size reports of unverified quality (e.g. marketdataforecast.com).
All URLs here are search-result-derived and unverified for liveness; several sites (Euromoney, American Banker, Celent) are bot-defended and may return 403 to automated fetches without being dead.
